answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a plume as the anchor of the cost.
